Inherited retinal dystrophy; no evidence of extraocular disease.

Umbrella skeletal dysplasia affecting bone and cartilage development; additional organ damage is not established across subtypes.
Squamous epithelial malignancy; skin assignment is provisional because the histologic definition does not specify an origin and includes noncutaneous tumours.
Hypomyelinating neurodevelopmental disease; contractures and kyphoscoliosis each 2/4; gingival overgrowth 2/4 supports oral involvement.
Meningeal tumour of the sphenocavernous region; ocular damage is not established in at least 30%.
Glycosylation disorder defined by neurodevelopmental disease and gastric bleeding; hearing loss 30-79%. Visual impairment may be cerebral.
Retinal degeneration with progressive visual loss in 3/3; retinal vessel attenuation remains within the ocular axis.
Corneal dystrophy causing recurrent erosions and progressive visual loss.
HDL metabolism disorder; atherosclerosis is a separate disease, and storage-related organ injury is subtype-specific.
Auditory neuropathy causes sensorineural hearing dysfunction; no generalized neurologic disease is established.
Iron-deficiency anemia and esophageal webs with dysphagia are obligatory defining features; nail changes occur in only 5-29%.
Menstrual disorder; an endocrine cause or endocrine gland damage is not inherent in this symptom-defined concept.
Alveolar proteinosis and immunodeficiency define disease. Splenomegaly 4/4 and leukocytosis do not establish destructive hematologic disease.
Tuberculous infection destroys vertebrae; spinal cord injury and pulmonary disease are not inherent or consistently common.
Tumour originates in the fourth cranial nerve; impaired eye movement does not establish direct ocular tissue damage.

Immune-mediated inflammatory dermatosis of vulvar skin with sclerosis and fibrosis; genital location does not exclude the skin axis.
Partial trisomy 1 syndromes commonly cause developmental delay/intellectual disability; other malformations depend on the duplicated segment.
Isolated developmental eye disorder with microphthalmia and high hypermetropia in 9/9.
Secondary dysfunction of central motor pathways causing parkinsonism; no additional organ involvement is intrinsic to the umbrella concept.
Red-cell membrane disorder causing hemolytic anemia; pigment gallstones are a separately diagnosed complication.
Severe long-QT syndrome defines cardiac involvement; developmental impairment is common (>30%) in the classic Timothy type 2 phenotype.
Motor neuron disease with muscle atrophy; contractures and clubfeet in 2/2. Respiratory failure reflects muscle weakness rather than direct lung damage.
